Literally it is false in those representatives: under the tail event the signed first meridian angle is negative with probability 1/2 by simultaneous reversal, and on that half the original v1 is close to 2π. The nonnegative v2 then makes the scaled first component escape. The complete replacement RESULT.md explicitly wraps both meridian angles and the relative longitude and is correct. Equality in the ambient triangle bound localizes precisely at antipodal outer-equator pairs; direct expansion gives the three positive coefficients 2r(R+r), 2rR, (R+r)^2, and reversal removes cubic terms. The exact deficit threshold is 4(R+r)ε−ε²; ellipsoid sandwiching changes volume by O(ε^(5/2)). The local probability density is (R+r)^2/(8π³R²) and the ellipsoid volume is 16π ε^(3/2)/(3r√R), giving the stated coefficient. Scaling those same ellipsoids and the density proves the repaired conditional law, independently of the uniform initial longitude. The log derivative (2k−5)/(2k(k+1)) gives the minimum and multiplicity; at fixed diameter the two shapes have distinct surface area. An independently written exact-azimuth Gauss–Legendre integration at R=2.5,r=1 gave probability/leading-term ratios 0.9997484 and 0.9999827 (96-point rule, ε=0.02 and 0.005); this corroborates the coefficient only.
